chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abu Shibl, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A Muslim man was tried, so he committed fornication with the slave girl of his brother. So what is his repentance?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He goes to him and informs him, and asks him to make that a permissibility for him, and he does not repeat.'

He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'Supposing he does not make a permissibility for him from that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He meets Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and he is an adulterer, a betrayer.'

I said, 'So the Fire is his destination?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The intercession of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and our intercession is nullified by your sins, O group of the Shias! Therefore, do not keep repeating (your sins) and rely upon our intercession.'
For by Allah, he will not attain our intercession when he indulges in this until he is hit by the pain of the Punishment and sees the horrors of Hell.
ai.seo_question: What is the process of repentance for fornication with a slave girl and how does intercession work?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the distinction between divine forgiveness and the rights of others (haqq al-adam) in cases of fornication with a slave girl, emphasizing that the brother's consent is crucial for the sin to be lifted. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a profound theological insight by linking the nullification of intercession (shafa'ah) to persistent reliance on it without repentance, warning that the 'people of the Shia' must not become complacent. The narrative underscores that intercession is conditional upon enduring the consequences of one's actions, serving as a corrective to popular misconceptions of automatic salvation.
